insight.title: Why You Find New Problems After Solving Old Ones
insight.subtitle: How your brain creates stress even when things are going well

sections.text: Have you noticed that life gets easier, but your stress stays the same? Your brain has a hidden system for finding trouble. As big problems vanish, your mind simply lowers its standards for "problems."

When actual threats disappear, your mind lowers its threshold for what qualifies as a crisis. You don’t necessarily have more trouble; you’ve simply expanded your definition of it to keep your brain occupied.
This explains why a slight delay or a minor critique feels like a disaster on an otherwise perfect day. We often mistake a calm environment for a new set of emergencies that aren’t there.
When you notice a minor annoyance today, ask if it's a real problem or just a perception shift.
High standards for your life should not require a low threshold for your peace of mind.
